title: Set up the emergency override passphrase
purpose: Sets up the emergency override (break-glass) passphrase of one PIM Manager environment: stores its SHA-256 hash as a secret in the environment's key vault, gives the Manager's managed identity read access to that one secret, and points the Manager at the vault.
whenToRun: Once per environment, before the emergency override is needed (Settings > Emergency override shows 'no emergency passcode configured' until it has run), and again to change the passphrase. Ring 1 first.

runAs.name: Key Vault Secrets Officer (or Key Vault Administrator)
runAs.why: Writes the secret PIM-EmergencyPasscode and reads it back.

runAs.name: User Access Administrator or Role Based Access Control Administrator (or Owner)
runAs.scope: the environment's key vault (the grant is made on one secret in it)
runAs.why: Creates the Azure role assignment that lets the Manager read that one secret.

runAs.name: Contributor (or Container Apps Contributor)
runAs.scope: the resource group of the Manager container app
runAs.why: Reads the Manager app and sets its PIM_EmergencyVault setting (a new revision).

changes.object: secret PIM-EmergencyPasscode (-SecretName) holding the SHA-256 hex of the passphrase; a new version when it already exists
changes.why: The Manager checks a typed passphrase against this hash. The clear passphrase is never stored, never on a command line, never logged.
changes.undo: Disable or delete the secret version in the key vault (break-glass activation is then refused until it is set again).

changes.object: the Manager container app's managed identity (system- and/or user-assigned)
changes.scope: the one secret <vault>/secrets/PIM-EmergencyPasscode (not the whole vault)
changes.why: So the Manager can read the hash -- least privilege: read access to that secret only. An existing grant on the vault or the secret is left alone.
changes.undo: Remove that role assignment on the secret (Azure portal > key vault > Secrets > the secret > Access control).

changes.object: environment variable PIM_EmergencyVault=<vault> on the Manager container app (read-modify-write; every other setting kept)
changes.scope: the Manager container app (-ManagerApp), a new revision
changes.why: Tells the Manager which vault holds the passphrase.
changes.undo: Remove PIM_EmergencyVault from the container app (a new revision).

changes.object: the result file named by -OutFile (never the passphrase or its hash)
changes.why: For a caller that reads the outcome.

parameters.name: ResourceGroup
parameters.help: The resource group of the Manager container app.

parameters.name: ContainerName
parameters.help: The Manager's container, when the app has more than one.

parameters.name: VaultName
parameters.help: The environment's own key vault (must use Azure RBAC authorization).

parameters.name: SecretName
parameters.help: The secret name the Manager reads.

parameters.name: Passphrase
parameters.help: The passphrase as a SecureString (at least 12 characters). Omit it to be prompted twice. Never plain text.

parameters.name: UseSignedInAccount
parameters.help: Sign in as the az user (asserted to be a user in -TenantId and -SubscriptionId). The recommended way.

parameters.name: AdminAppId
parameters.help: Automation: the admin application's client id (with -AdminCertThumbprint).

parameters.name: AdminCertThumbprint
parameters.help: Automation: the thumbprint of the admin application's certificate in the local machine store.

parameters.name: OutFile
parameters.help: Write the outcome as JSON to this file.

readsOnly: the Manager container app (its managed identities and environment variables)
the key vault (exists, uses Azure RBAC authorization) and its role assignments
whether the secret already exists (to say CREATE or REPLACE)
whatIf: Asks for no passphrase. Signs in, reads the Manager app, the vault and its role assignments, and prints each change it would make: 'What if: would CREATE (or REPLACE) secret PIM-EmergencyPasscode in <vault>', 'What if: would GRANT Key Vault Secrets User on secret PIM-EmergencyPasscode to the Manager identity <id>', 'What if: would SET PIM_EmergencyVault=<vault> on <app> (new revision)'. Nothing is written.
undo: Remove the Key Vault Secrets User role assignment on the secret, remove PIM_EmergencyVault from the Manager container app, and disable or delete the secret. Emergency override activation is then refused until the script runs again.
